acceptance_profile.description: Level 2 — Advanced. Pre-specified acceptance limits for the complete HRV robustness protocol.

context_of_use: Deterministic synthetic engineering QA for ECG R-peak detection, NN interval reconstruction, time-domain HRV and VLF/LF/HF metric implementations.

limitations: Synthetic signals do not establish clinical sensitivity, specificity, population generalization, or diagnostic safety.
A PASS applies only to the exact package, evidence level, verifier, algorithm build, submission, and hashes recorded in the evidence bundle.
The cited sources inform design and interpretation; none directly specifies the complete Synsigra case matrix and numeric gate set.
evidence_basis.numeric_threshold_basis: Pack-author pre-specified engineering gates selected for discrimination, regression stability, and the exact deterministic protocol; no numeric gate is copied from a cited standard or study.
evidence_basis.rationale: Metric definitions, five-minute spectral cases, NN exclusions, and explicit preprocessing traceability follow established HRV measurement concerns. Numeric comparison and acceptance limits are deterministic engineering regression gates.

sources.citation: Task Force of the European Society of Cardiology and the North American Society of Pacing and Electrophysiology. Circulation. 1996;93(5):1043-1065. PMID:8598068.
sources.limitation: It does not define implementation-error PASS/FAIL thresholds for a deterministic synthetic verifier.
sources.relevance: Defines standard HRV terminology, time- and frequency-domain metrics, frequency bands, and short-term recording conventions.
sources.title: Heart rate variability: standards of measurement, physiological interpretation and clinical use

sources.citation: Jarrin DC et al. Int J Psychophysiol. 2012;86(1):88-97. doi:10.1016/j.ijpsycho.2012.07.004.
sources.limitation: Its inter-software ICC results are not per-metric numerical error limits for Synsigra's exact synthetic truth.
sources.relevance: Demonstrates that processing choices affect cross-software HRV agreement, with especially poor VLF correspondence.
sources.title: Measurement fidelity of heart rate variability signal processing: the devil is in the details

sources.citation: Salo MA et al. Ann Noninvasive Electrocardiol. 2001;6(1):5-17. PMID:11174857.
sources.limitation: It does not prescribe Synsigra's NN exclusion policy or numerical acceptance gates.
sources.relevance: Shows that ectopic-beat editing method and burden materially affect time- and frequency-domain HRV results.
sources.title: Ectopic beats in heart rate variability analysis: effects of editing on time and frequency domain measures

sources.citation: Reklewski W, Miskowicz M. Sensors. 2024;24(5):1698. doi:10.3390/s24051698.
sources.limitation: Its tested detectors, signals, noise injection, and tolerances differ from Synsigra and do not define Synsigra gate values.
sources.relevance: Shows that reported QRS performance changes with temporal tolerance, noise level, and morphology, supporting explicit multidimensional protocol disclosure.
sources.title: QRS Detector Performance Evaluation Aware of Temporal Accuracy and Presence of Noise

evidence_boundary: Synthetic engineering evidence only; not clinical autonomic validation, patient-population evidence, diagnostic performance evidence, or a substitute for sponsor-specific protocol and representative clinical data.

evidence_profile.description: The curated pack's reviewed engineering acceptance gates for mature implementations. This is the recommended default.
evidence_profile.threshold_adjustment: The pack author's reviewed baseline thresholds are used unchanged.

truth_policy.event_scoreability: R-peak truth requires complete in-record QRS support and more than 5% retained signal during all-lead dropout; additive and severe noise remain scoreable stress.
truth_policy.exclusion: Ectopic, artifact-overlapping and otherwise rejected intervals and their adjacent intervals are explicitly excluded; excluded intervals are never bridged for successive-difference metrics.
truth_policy.interval_definition: NN intervals are derived from consecutive accepted construction R peaks.
truth_policy.negative_case: The hrv_short_window_rejected scenario remains an assembly-time range-rejection test and is not an executable evidence-matrix case.
truth_policy.spectral_window: Frequency-domain truth requires at least 300 seconds and uses the declared metric-definition interpolation policy.
